name: CyberGym
intro: CyberGym是一个大规模基准测试，旨在评估AI智能体在真实世界网络安全方面的能力。它包含1,507个真实漏洞，涵盖188个软件项目。该基准主要任务是让智能体根据文本描述和代码库生成漏洞复现的概念验证测试。CyberGym不仅能有效区分AI智能体的网络安全能力，还促成了35个零日漏洞的发现。
build_method: 从 OSS-Fuzz/ARVO 历史漏洞定位精确补丁提交，提取修复前后代码、标准 PoC 与补丁，用 GPT-4.1 改写描述并经信息充分性、双版本复现和堆栈去重筛选
metric: PoC 成功率：修复前版本必须触发 sanitizer 崩溃，修复后版本必须不崩溃
build_method_en: Source OSS-Fuzz/ARVO vulnerabilities, locate exact fix commits, recover pre/post code, ground-truth PoC and patch, rephrase descriptions with GPT-4.1, then filter for informativeness, dual-version reproducibility and stack-trace uniqueness
intro_en: CyberGym is a large-scale benchmark designed to evaluate AI agents' capabilities in real-world cybersecurity. It includes 1,507 real vulnerabilities across 188 software projects. The main task is for agents to generate proof-of-concept tests reproducing vulnerabilities based on textual descriptions and codebases. CyberGym effectively differentiates AI agents' cybersecurity skills and has contributed to the discovery of 35 zero-day vulnerabilities.

drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2506.02548 Sections 3–5 and the official sunblaze-ucb/cybergym release. CyberGym sources historical vulnerabilities and ground-truth PoCs from OSS-Fuzz through ARVO. Because OSS-Fuzz updates projects daily, the authors binary-search commits in the final pre-fix day to find the first version where the ground-truth PoC stops crashing. Each candidate yields pre-patch and post-patch code, the ground-truth PoC and patch; sanitizer-enabled executables are built, and GPT-4.1 rephrases informative single-issue patch messages into vulnerability descriptions. Quality assurance removes vague or multi-issue descriptions, re-runs the PoC on both versions to verify reproducibility, and removes redundant/ambiguous cases using patch identity and crash-stack similarity. The final benchmark has 1,507 instances across 188 projects. Difficulty Level 0 provides only code, Level 1—the primary task—adds the description, Level 2 adds the ground-truth crash stack, and Level 3 adds the patch diff and post-patch code. Agents iteratively submit PoCs and observe execution feedback. A success must crash the pre-patch executable under sanitizers and not crash the post-patch executable; success rate is the fraction of instances meeting both conditions. Separate from the benchmark metric, follow-up analysis finds 17 incomplete historical patches and 10 zero-days from benchmark-generated PoCs, then 25 additional zero-days in open-ended latest-version runs, for 35 responsibly disclosed zero-days total.
